LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 4.1.1 SELF- EXPRESSION: PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 4.1: Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Self- expression: Pronunciation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Self- expression: Pronunciation. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we demonstrate attentive listening?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary from a story for comprehension
2. construct sentences using vocabulary and adverbs correctly for expression

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Self- expression: Pronunciation helps you communicate well at school and at home.

• Listen with your eyes and ears. Face the speaker and wait for your turn.

• When you speak, use a clear voice and polite words.

• Practise short dialogues with a partner using Kenyan school situations.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short instruction, then repeat it to a friend in your own words.

Example 3: Role-play buying an item at the market using polite requests: “Please…”, “Thank you.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Practise a 30-second greeting dialogue with a partner.
2. Listen to three instructions and carry them out in order.
3. Tell a short news item from your day using complete sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Teach a younger learner one polite greeting from this lesson.
2. Write five sentences you can say when welcoming a visitor at school.
3. Ask a parent to give you three oral instructions; write them down after listening.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Listen to a story based on the theme and identify vocabulary related to the theme,
2. Make sentences using vocabulary identified,
3. Work jointly to make a presentation using vocabulary identified,
4. Team up to sing songs commonly used in ceremonies and festivals,
5. Creativity and Imagination: The learner embraces creative ideas when making presentations based on the theme.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we demonstrate attentive listening?
2. When do we use adverbs?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Good listeners look, wait, and respond.
2. Clear speech helps others understand you.
3. Polite language shows respect.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
